instructions:
NEVER run git stash, git checkout, git reset, git restore, git clean, git merge, git rebase or any command that changes the index, the stash stack, or other worktrees' state. Do NOT touch crates/ajax-web/web/ or any code. DO NOT EXPLORE the code base: all facts are below. Read ONLY the four allowed docs, and only around the lines named. Edit the docs in your first substantive action, then run the verify commands. Do not commit.

FACTS ABOUT THE PI RPC TRANSPORT (all verified in code and tests; document exactly this, invent nothing):
- Pi is no longer reached through the `pi-acp` bridge. Ajax runs `pi --mode rpc -na [--session <id>]` as a child process and speaks Pi's JSONL RPC mode over its stdio (one JSON object per LF-terminated line; framing splits on LF only). The transport is chosen by core's launch table: `AcpLaunch.transport` is `HarnessTransport::PiRpc` for Pi and `HarnessTransport::Acp` for Cursor, Codex and Claude. Cursor, Codex and Claude are unchanged and still use ACP (Cursor natively; Codex/Claude through their bridge packages).
- Pi stays a chat-capable harness: `acp_launch_for_agent(Pi)` still returns Some (that predicate is the "supports Ajax Chat" test across the code base).
- Install: `npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (provides the `pi` binary). `ajax doctor` reports it as `rpc:pi` (checks the `pi` binary; the message names the install command when it is missing); it no longer reports `acp:pi`. Codex and Claude keep `acp:codex` / `acp:claude` for their bridges.
- Handshake: on spawn Ajax sends get_state, get_available_models, get_available_thinking_levels and get_commands, correlated by id; get_state (with data.sessionId) is required, the other three degrade to empty lists.
- Session identity: Pi's own session id IS the Ajax session id (the id `pi-acp` used to hand out was already Pi's native id, so stored sessions keep resuming). Restore relaunches with `--session <id>`; fail-closed: if Pi comes back with a different session id the spawn fails with the typed `ACP restore unavailable` error (Retry / Start fresh) and never silently starts a fresh session.
- Model and thinking level: Pi's models are advertised as one `model` select whose values are `provider/id`; thinking levels come from get_available_thinking_levels and are advertised as a `thought_level` select (category ThoughtLevel). Changes go through Pi's `set_model` (provider + modelId) and `set_thinking_level`. A persisted pin has the same form as for other harnesses: `provider/id|thought_level=high`. A pin that cannot be applied is reported as a model-apply error and does not fail the spawn; later steps of the pin still apply.
- Usage: after each finished prompt Ajax calls Pi's get_session_stats (2 second cap) and emits a context-usage update (contextUsage.tokens / contextWindow) BEFORE the finish event, so the live head meter works; if the stats are missing the finish is delivered without a usage update. This replaces the pi-acp-specific usage behavior.
- Cancel maps to Pi's `abort`; the run ends with stopReason `cancelled`. Run completion is Pi's `agent_settled` event.
- Permissions and elicitation: Ajax launches Pi with `-na` (no approve), so Pi RPC mode surfaces no permission or form-elicitation requests to the browser; the Pi variant rejects permission/elicitation responses.
- Known gaps (state them as such): image/audio prompt blocks are not forwarded to Pi yet (a placeholder line is sent); Pi extension UI records (setStatus, setWidget, ...) are ignored.
- Model catalog for Pi comes from the RPC handshake, not from an ACP session/new.
- Files for orientation: crates/ajax-web/src/adapters/web_session_acp/{pi_rpc_process,pi_rpc_handshake,pi_rpc_session,pi_rpc_map,pi_rpc_client,session_client}.rs.
